We received the notice about the upcoming maintenance window for our private VPC cluster. A few asks from our side before we lock dates:

- Rollback SLA: if the upgrade causes degraded inference latency beyond our SLA, what is the target time to rollback to the previous image?

We also want a dry-run / canary window with our oncall present. Proposed week: Dec 2–6, prefer UTC-friendly times (02:00–06:00 UTC).

Sanjay — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by the full runbook and schedule (attached).

- Version pinning: your workloads will remain pinned to the minor version you currently run (v3.8.x). We will only roll forward pinned workloads with explicit written authorization from your team. For autoscaling pools we manage, we'll apply non-breaking security micro-patches only if you opt in; otherwise they will be staged in a canary cluster.

- Network changes: no control-plane IP changes are required for this patch sequence. The only network diffs are egress ACL tightening on port 9000 (reducing a wide-open range to your CIDR block) and a BGP next-hop update for the canary segment. Both changes are listed in routing-change-diff.patch attached. We will apply ACL changes during the scheduled low-traffic window and validate reachability before user traffic resumes.

- Rollback SLA: target TTR (time-to-restore) is 30 minutes for full cluster rollback to the prior image (we consider 30–45min worst-case including dataplane KV warm-up). Our rollback checklist is attached (rollback_checklist.md) and includes automated job triggers and guardrail checks.

Proposed schedule for dry-run canary: Dec 3 03:00–05:00 UTC (we will run one canary wave then a short telemetry hold). If that looks green, we schedule a broader wave in your next maintenance window (Dec 5 02:00–06:00 UTC).

Attached: vpc_maintenance_window_template.xlsx (proposed timing), rollback_checklist.md, routing-change-diff.patch

Can you confirm the canary slot and your oncall contact for the dry run?

Thanks —

Subject: Internal: ACM canary + rollback plan (need L1/L2 owners)

Team — looping you in after Sanjay's note. Things we need to lock before Dec 3 canary:

1) Owners: L1 oncall (verify runbooks), L2 escalation (DB/serving), network lead for ACL/BGP change.
2) Canary traffic profile: run 10% of production qps against the canary cluster for 30 minutes, then validate token-level latency P50/P95 and error-rate.
3) Automated rollback triggers: P95 latency > 250ms for 3 consecutive 1-min windows OR request error-rate delta > 0.5%. These are in rollback_checklist.md but callout them here.
4) Audit and evidence: capture packet captures for the ACL change, and a pre/post KV cache hit-rate snapshot. Attach artifacts to JIRA: INFRA-8421.
5) Communication template: Ben will confirm to customer. Monica to prepare the incident bridge and recording.

Please reply with confirmed owners and any additional gating metrics by EOD 2029-11-30.

Thanks,
Ben

Ben / folks — I can take L2 escalation and own the rollback automation. Quick technical notes and clarifications:

- Rollback path: we will use the image-swap mechanism at the orchestrator layer which preserves persistent KV stores. Pre-checks will snapshot KV keys for 10 minutes prior to image swap; post-rollback we run a checksum on critical KV prefixes.
- Network guard: Vivek, can you validate the ACL change will not affect our monitoring collectors (port 9100) and the control-plane health probes? If so we can mark the change low-risk.
- Canary validation: add a QoS check for tokenization latency (sub-component) — if tokenizer P95 regresses > 15% we auto-abort.

Owners: L1 oncall = Monica Patel; L2 = Karthik Iyer; Network = Vivek Kulkarni. I'll prepare the rollback playbook as an executable job and post the runbook to the Jira by 12/2.

Karthik
